title: Singing Wineglass Robot
overview: Automated robot exploring acoustic robotics and mechanical tuning by driving controlled friction across wineglass rims to produce musical tones.
scope: Acoustic iteration, mechanical design, and tuning of sponge pressure, moisture levels, air density, and structural rigidity.
materials:
• Wineglasses (tuned by fill level or size, one per note)
 • Mechanical drive components for rim-friction actuation
 • Sponge or contact material for the rim interface
 • Structural frame/components for rigidity
fabricationSteps:
1. Select wineglasses and determine their individual resonant notes.
 2. Design and build a mechanism that drives a sponge or contact material around each glass's rim with controlled pressure.
 3. Mount the mechanism(s) in a rigid frame — structural rigidity strongly affects tone quality.
 4. Tune each glass individually: adjust sponge pressure, sponge dampness, rim dampness, and the air density/volume ratio inside the glass until it reliably sings its note.
 5. Attempt to run multiple glasses simultaneously and identify cross-glass interference or timing issues.
 6. Document which combinations of pressure/moisture/rigidity settings produced the most reliable single-glass tone, for future multi-glass tuning work.
outcome: Successfully demonstrated pitch control across individual glasses with complete media documentation and technical reflections.
